$comment: The Technology catalogue of the migration path (docs/MODERNIZATION.md): technologies that keep OBDX as it is. pack names the target pack under target-packs/ that writes it; a technology is ready only when that pack is in the factory. The numbers of rules, templates and starter files are read from the pack itself.

packVersions: First release: screens, forms, service calls and tests
technologies.name: React + TypeScript
technologies.text: Widely used, large ecosystem, runs beside the JET screens module by module.
technologies.meta: Static build served through Oracle HTTP Server
points: Same OBDX REST services, session cookie and nonce
Strong component libraries and accessibility tooling
limits: Keep the JET chart in a wrapper, or rebuild it

packVersions: First release: screens, forms, service calls and tests
technologies.name: React Native
technologies.text: One code base for iOS and Android, with the same services as internet banking.
points: Same OBDX REST services and server-driven 2FA
Native look on iOS and Android
Shares the bank design system's tokens
limits: Rebuild with the pack's spending chart

packVersions: First release: standalone screens with signal forms and tests
technologies.name: Angular
technologies.text: A full framework with forms, routing and testing built in; suits large teams.
technologies.meta: Static build served through Oracle HTTP Server
points: Same OBDX REST services, session cookie and nonce
Material and the CDK for accessible components
Strong typing and testing built in
limits: Keep the JET chart in a wrapper

technologies.name: JET Core Pack
technologies.text: Oracle JET's newer components, for banks that stay with Oracle JET but leave Knockout.
points: The premium JET pack's Core Pack build

technologies.name: Vue 3
technologies.text: Light and quick to learn; a good fit for smaller teams.
technologies.meta: Static build served through Oracle HTTP Server
points: Same OBDX REST services, session cookie and nonce
limits: The pack's components fill the gap

technologies.name: Flutter
technologies.text: One code base for iOS and Android with its own rendering.
points: Same OBDX REST services and server-driven 2FA
limits: Flutter Web is not offered: see below
A new language for most bank teams

technologies.name: Swift and Kotlin
technologies.text: Fully native iOS and Android apps, two code bases.
limits: Twice the screens to build and test

technologies.name: Capacitor
technologies.text: Wraps the React or Angular web app as a mobile app.
points: One team for web and mobile
limits: Web screens in a native shell

notOffered: It puts a new server in front of OBDX that would hold the bank's session cookie. A static React build is offered instead.
It draws on a canvas and its screen-reader support is off by default.
Few bank teams can staff or support them.
connects: Calls the same digx/v1 REST services with the same request and response
Unchanged: no new API, no new server
Sends the OBDX session cookie on every call, through OHS
The same login and session as the JET app
Asks for a nonce and sends it with every request
Shows the 2FA screen the server asks for, then retries
Decides when 2FA is needed, as today
Sends masked account tokens back; encrypts the password on screen
Shows the menus the server returns for the user
Carries over the labels, languages and field validations
Built to static files served by OHS beside the JET app
